about: ✎ PENCIL. Hand-maintained, read by queries.ts. Each query below is what the exhaustive enumeration (research/conformance/) observed on the date given: it names the finding and what would settle it, or, once `triaged` flips to true, the ruling itself, taking no other position on the cause. If findings/triage.json becomes the one home for a finding's status, fold `triaged` and `finding` into it.

defaults.$note: The expectation for any query not named below: the P1.3 properties as stated in issue #1, not observations.

CONFLICT/26b-id+30a.would_settle: Retired: colregs@0.2.2 answered this by changing 26b-id's relation to 30a from rel:excludes to rel:overrides (FIND-01's ruling). excludingPairs() no longer pairs them, so buildQueries() no longer produces this id at all -- kept here only as the historical record of the finding this settled, not as a live query. See findings/FIND-01.json.

CONFLICT/26c-id+30a.would_settle: Retired, same ruling as CONFLICT/26b-id+30a (FIND-02). See findings/FIND-02.json.

NO-OBLIGATION/any.would_settle: Settled: Rule 3(i) rules a vessel made fast to the shore out of Rule 30 entirely, prescribing no lights at all. run.ts EXPECTED_EMPTY_POSITIONS and its README record this ruling for position:moored; findings/triage.json no longer carries a separate entry for it.

NO-OBLIGATION/not-moored.observed_by: npm run conformance, check consistency-no-obligation, position breakdown: every zero-obligation record was position:moored
